title: Structure-aware fuzzing of the DER parsers
description:
## Why

A different failure class from everything the corpora cover. Conformance vectors and differential testing find WRONG VERDICTS; fuzzing finds panics, hangs and quadratic blowups. pkix-path already carries DoS guards written against that class (MAX_AVAS_PER_RDN, max_chain_certs, the O(n^2) duplicate scan ordering in check_inputs, and a 20 000-entry chain test), which is evidence the class is real here and currently guarded by hand-reasoning plus a few targeted tests.

## What

cargo-fuzz targets on the parse boundaries, not the whole validator:

* Certificate::from_der plus validate_path with a fixed anchor and policy.
* The name-constraint comparison functions, which are pure and take attacker-controlled strings and byte slices.
* CRL and OCSP response parsing in pkix-revocation.
* The AC parser in pkix-ac, which keeps a byte range into the original DER and is the newest code in the workspace.

Structure-aware rather than raw bytes: a raw fuzzer spends its whole budget failing the outer SEQUENCE. Either an Arbitrary impl that builds plausible TBSCertificates, or seed the corpus from PKITS/limbo/CT and let the mutator work from valid certificates.

## Acceptance

No panic, no unbounded loop, and no superlinear time on any input. A crash is a bug; a slow unit is a bug if the growth is superlinear in input size.

## Availability

Nothing to verify -- cargo-fuzz is tooling, not a corpus. Needs a nightly toolchain, which the MSRV job does not use, so this runs as its own job or not in CI at all.
